notesStmt.note: In a letter to Richard Maurice Bucke, dated November 10, 1888, Whitman writes that he has "finished the little beginning & end Notes I spoke of for the big book and sent to the printer." This proof was therefore made sometime after that date and the corrections shortly thereafter, likely sometime in mid-November 1888. Another extant proof contains corrections which are incorporated here, suggesting that the present corrections were made later.
A corrected proof of "Note at Beginning," which appeared between the title page and the table of contents of Whitman's Complete Poems & Prose (1888–9).

body.head: NOTE AT BEGINNING.
body.ab:
LEAVES OF GRASS,
with the brief Annex, SANDS AT SEVENTY, in November⁐ Boughs,
body.p: (When I had got this volume well under way, I was quite suddenly prostrated by illness—paralysis‸,/ continued yet—which will have to ‸serve as an to for as excuse ‸for many faults of both omission and commission in it.)

But I would not let the great and momentous eEra of these years, these States, slip away without attempting to arrest in a special printed book (as much in spirit as letter, and may‸⹀/ be for the future more than the present), ,)/ some few specimens—even vital throbs, breaths—as representations of it—all all—/from my point of view, and right from the midst of it, and at the time.

There is a tally‸⹀/ stamp and stage‸⹀/stage⹀result result of periods and nations, elusive, at second or third hand, often escaping the historian of matter-of-fact—in some sort the nation's spiritual formative ferment or chaos—the getting in of its essence, formulating identity—a law of it, and significant part of its progress. (Of the best of events and facts, even the most important, there are finally not the events and facts only, but something flashing out and fluctuating like tuft-flames or eidoólins, from all.) My going up and down amidst these years, and the impromptu jottings of their sights and thoughts, of war and peace, have been in accordance with that law, and probably a result of it. . . . In certain respects, (emotionality, passions, spirituality, the invisible trend,) I therefore launch forth ‸the divisions of the following book as not only a consequent of that period and its influences, but in one sort a History of America, the past 35 years, after the rest‸,/ and after the adjuncts of that history have been studied and attended to.
